Welcome. Have you ever wondered why so many leaders—no matter where or when—seem to get ahead by bending, or even breaking, the very rules they're meant to protect?
Together, we're about to pull back the curtain on the real forces at play in the world of politics. It's a world shaped by power, ambition, and the constant juggling of self-interest. And it turns out, as Bruce Bueno de Mesquita reveals in The Dictator's Handbook: Why Bad Behavior Is Almost Always Good Politics, the logic behind these moves isn't just about right or wrong—it's about survival.
So, what drives leaders to act the way they do? Why do coalitions, loyalty, and resource control matter so much, whether we're looking at democracies or dictatorships? As we explore these questions, you'll notice patterns and strategies that might just change the way you see politics—and maybe even the world around us.
Let's dive in together and discover how the mechanics of power really work, and what it means for all of us living under the rules—written and unwritten—set by those at the top.
Ready to see politics in a whole new light? Let's get started.
